edbDesc: (or Gibbs-Marangoni effect) The presence of a gradient in surface tension will naturally cause the liquid to flow away from regions of low surface tension. The surface tension gradient can be caused by concentration gradient or by a temperature gradient (surface tension is a function of temperature).
title: Marangoni effect
description: Liquid flows from where its surface tension is low toward where it is high, dragging the surface along: a drop of soap sends pepper racing to a dish's edge, and wine climbs a glass in 'tears'. James Thomson explained the tears in 1855 and Carlo Marangoni studied the effect in 1865.
effect: a liquid surface flows from low toward high surface tension
usedIn: Marangoni drying of silicon wafers with alcohol vapour
strength: A trace of soap clears pepper across a dish in a fraction of a second; surface flows reach centimetres per second.
pickWhy: Specific, named effect that moves and dries liquids; not in the deck.
